thread:
alex: Kicking off POC with ACME. Need help scoping success criteria + capacity. 3-week POC, goal = conversational assistant for support triage. They want ~95% answers under 800ms and a hard budget ~ $5k for the POC. Can SEs + SRE advise on token volumes, throughput, and realistic GPU sizing?
maria: Quick Qs: what's expected concurrent users / daily active agents, avg prompt length, and avg model output size? Also do they require full-gen answers (600+ tokens) or can we do short summaries/streams?
alex: Customer says ~200 daily agents, peak concurrent ~50. Typical conversation 4 messages per agent during a shift. Avg user input ~120 tokens, model generation ~600 tokens => ~720 tokens per request. They plan 8 active hours/day. They can provide 50 sample prompts for eval.
chris: Doing rough math to surface tradeoffs. Baseline daily tokens = 200 agents * 4 requests * 720 tokens = 576,000 tokens/day. For 3-week POC (~21 days) that's ~12.1M tokens. Peak concurrency risk: if 50 users fire near-simultaneously that's 50 concurrent requests.
chris: Latency perspective: 600 tokens generated per request. To hit 800ms end-to-end you'd need generation speed ~750 tok/s (600/0.8) which isn't realistic on a single GPU for a 13B-style model. So either reduce response length, accept higher SLO, or parallelize across many GPUs (expensive).
maria: Practical options for meeting their constraints:
- Option A: shorten responses to ~150-250 tokens (compressive summaries) + streaming; keeps quality but reduces tokens by ~60-75%.
- Option B: use a smaller model & retrieval + reranking so we return short top-k candidates rather than full long gens.
- Option C: provision burst H100 capacity for concurrent spikes and A100 for steady traffic (autoscale).

maria: For POC I'd recommend Option A (shorter answers + streaming) to prove UX within budget, then scale if they need longer generative outputs.
alex: Good. Can you give a ballpark GPU + cost estimate for both baseline + peak burst? Toni needs numbers for the quote.
chris: Ballpark on-demand rates (example): L4 ~ $3/hr, A100 ~ $20/hr, H100 ~ $40/hr. Generation throughput (very approximate): L4 ~ 25-40 tok/s, A100 ~ 50-80 tok/s, H100 ~ 120-250 tok/s (depends on quantization & model).
chris: Using those numbers: if we target 250-token responses (instead of 600) then per-request tokens ~370 (120 in + 250 out). At peak 50 concurrent, worst-case concurrent generation work = 50 * 250 = 12,500 generated tokens. If a single A100 can do ~60 tok/s => aggregate capacity per A100 ~60 tok/s. To serve 12,500 generated tokens within 1 second you'd need ~209 GPUs (impractical). But if we accept 5s p95 latency, need capacity such that generated tokens/sec >= 12,500/5 = 2,500 tok/s => ~42 A100-equivalent GPUs. Still high.
chris: Key takeaway: strict 800ms p95 with 200-600 token outputs for 50 concurrent users isn't realistic w/o huge infra. We need to reduce output size or accept higher latency or reduce concurrency bursts.

toni: From budget side, $5k POC cap with 21 days and 8 hours/day => 168 GPU-hours max if using H100 at $30/hr -> that's ~$5k only for H100 runtime. Realistically we should design POC to run mostly on cheaper GPUs (A100/L4) and only burst to H100 for brief tests.

maria: Recommended POC plan (minimal risk / within $5k):
- Phase 1 (week 1): smoke tests. Use L4 instances for dev + small evals, get sample prompts and run 1k evals to measure token distribution.
- Phase 2 (week 2): constrained UX test. Reduce generation to 150-250 tokens, enable streaming; provision 1-2 A100 nodes for steady load, and configure autoscale that can spin up H100 for short (minutes-hours) bursts.
- Phase 3 (week 3): collect QA metrics, run customer eval set (50 prompts x multiple modalities), measure p50/p95 token latencies and cost.

maria: Quick example config we'd deploy for POC (pseudo):
```
model: redwood/edge-13b-8bit
response_limit: 250
streaming: true
autoscale: { steady: 2 x A100, burst_policy: scale_to 4 x H100 for 10m windows }
metrics: collect token_count, gen_time_ms, p50_p95
```

alex: That looks good. Customer ok with shorter responses if we surface a "more detail" button that triggers longer generations asynchronously. Will share sample prompts tomorrow.
chris: Action items:
- Maria: run 1k-sample eval on L4 and A100, attach token histograms and per-token gen speed by model variant.
- Toni: draft POC quote with 3 scenarios (L4-only, A100 steady + H100 burst, H100-heavy) and hourly rates + estimated hours.
- Alex: get the 50 sample prompts and confirm whether streaming is acceptable for UX.

alex: Timeline: can we have draft quote + eval results by EOD Friday? Customer wants to start next Wednesday.
maria: Yes, I can run the evals and post results by Thursday EOD. Toni will post the quote by Friday AM.
chris: I'll put a rough autoscale policy and safety limits in the POC to avoid runaway cost. deploy-bot: POC sandbox cluster created -> cluster-id: poc-acme-42.
toni: I'll keep the quote conservative and add an optional extra for H100 burst testing.
alex: Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll sync with ACME and push sample prompts.
